O1.citation: “Re-run all three golden cases against the edited skill” and “A and C verify the edit caused no regressions.”

O2.citation: “Each case needs a fresh, context-free runner that sees only its input. Judges see only the resulting artifact, that case’s original bar, and the skill’s first principles.” This separates runners from evidence-based judges, but does not explicitly require repetitions.

O3.citation: Evidence is missing: the artifact requires neither repeated trials nor per-case pass rates sufficient to reveal nondeterminism.

O4.citation: The artifact asks to “Report the original B gap, the defect it mapped to, [and] the edit made,” but does not require diagnosing any new miss as a skill defect versus a bad case or repeating the diagnose-revise-full-sweep loop.

O5.citation: “Report the original B gap, the defect it mapped to, the edit made, and the before/after results for all cases,” with “each result includ[ing] cited evidence against its own bar.”

S1.citation: The smell is absent: the artifact explicitly says, “Re-run all three golden cases.”

S2.citation: The smell is absent: “Each case needs a fresh, context-free runner that sees only its input.”

S3.citation: The smell is absent: runners produce artifacts while separate “Judges see only the resulting artifact” and evaluation bar.

S4.citation: The smell is absent: the artifact requires “before/after results for all cases,” not merely an aggregate score, although it fails to require repeated-trial pass rates.

S5.citation: The smell is absent: “A and C verify the edit caused no regressions,” and success requires that “A and C still pass.”

rationale: The artifact correctly requires a fresh full sweep of A, B, and C, separates blind runners from evidence-based judges, and demands case-level cited before/after evidence. It is incomplete because it does not require enough repetitions to calculate per-case pass rates, and it omits the diagnose-as-skill-defect-versus-bad-case, revise, and full-sweep loop for new misses.
